Tehran has demanded that vessels seek permission to transit the strait, insisting there will be no return to the pre-war system of unrestricted navigation.

Iran has repeatedly insisted that it will not reopen Hormuz until the US meets its demands.
d4ec602d6e751e6f: On Tuesday, Google announced AlphaGenome Atlas, a resource that attempts to predict the consequences of every possible single-base variant in the human genome. The human genome is about 3 billion bases long, so trying the other three DNA bases that don't appear in our reference genome means sending a total of 9 billion bases through AlphaGenome software.

AlphaGenome is designed to identify potential functions of non-coding DNA, which does not encode proteins but makes up the vast majority of the human genome. Some of this non-coding DNA is essential for controlling the activity of the protein-coding portion—it tells the cell where and when to make messenger RNAs, how to process them into mature protein-coding forms, and so on. But much of it appears to be little more than the remains of viruses and other molecular parasites.

Being able to identify the functional portion is very useful, as is having all the analysis done by a single software package. But until biologists start to use it heavily (assuming they do), it won't be clear what AlphaGenome offers beyond what we could have gotten out of its training data.
bc00331207a0265e: MADRID: Spain recorded 61 days under heatwave conditions across the mainland and Balearic Islands in 2026, the highest number on record and far above the previous peak of 41 days in 2022, national weather agency AEMET said on Wednesday.

Spain also experienced its hottest summer since records began in 1961, with an average temperature of 24.5 degrees Celsius, 0.3 degrees above the previous record set in 2025 and 2.4 degrees above the 1991-2020 average.

Four heatwaves affected mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands, including a six-day episode in early September, AEMET said, meaning that Spain experienced extremely high temperatures on approximately two out of every three days of the summer.
The most intense heatwave, lasting most of July, affected 37 provinces and a temperature anomaly of 3.9C was recorded.
The July and August heatwaves, lasting 23 and 24 days respectively, were among the longest on record since at least 1975.
The September episode affected 16 provinces and was the fifth heatwave recorded in that month since records began.
The Canary Islands experienced a separate five-day heatwave in August.

AEMET said the summer-like conditions extended beyond June, July and August, with July-level temperatures across large parts of Spain in late May and the heatwave during the meteorological autumn in September.
Spain's 10 hottest summers on record have all occurred in the 21st century, while seven of the eight hottest have occurred since 2015.

Data on the Health Ministry's daily mortality monitoring system MoMo showed that 5,234 people are thought to have died from heat-related causes between May 15 and Aug 31, the highest toll recorded for the summer period since the monitoring system was launched in 2015.
Scientists say extreme weather events are becoming more frequent due to human-caused climate change.
cf461d3643a91c83: WASHINGTON: Defence startup Covenant on Wednesday unveiled a heavy-payload, long-range cruise missile it says can be quickly mass-produced at a relatively low cost, in the latest challenge to major US weapons makers from some of Silicon Valley's biggest investors.

The announcement from Covenant after two years of development coincides with efforts by the US and its allies to restock missile inventories with less expensive and plentiful long-range precision-strike missiles after the war in Iran depleted stocks of the critical armaments.

Its missile, called Anthem, is a ground-launched cruise missile carrying a payload of more than 200kg. In a fight, it would be used in high volumes to work alongside other long-range missiles like the 1,609km range Tomahawk cruise missile produced by RTX's Raytheon unit and the 965km Lockheed Martin Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile-Extended Range (JASSM-ER).

Comparable weapons from the biggest defence contractors are "being built in small quantities at really high prices. And so we set out to change that," Michael Kaufman, Covenant's co-founder and CEO, told Reuters in an interview.

The company, founded in 2024, has raised just over US$250 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux, 8VC, Aleph and Lightspeed, and now employs more than 200 people across the US, Germany and Israel.
Anthem is powered by a solid rocket motor for takeoff and a heavy-fuel jet engine for cruise flight. Covenant says it has flown the missile more than 200 times over the past year in tests.
Executives said the missile was built with an eye toward the Pacific. "We were designed for the China fight," said Covenant President Abby Denburg.

Military planners envision using ground-launched weapons designed to strike from allied islands near China, such as the Philippines — a stretch of roughly 3218km that would put Chinese targets within range without relying on manned aircraft or naval strike groups.

Covenant is targeting a mid-six-figure price per missile once at full-rate production. The company has already booked roughly US$150 million in orders and expects to begin generating revenue in 2027 as deliveries ramp up.
An international customer is due to begin taking delivery of German-built Anthems by the end of this year, with US Army deliveries expected in 2027, executives said.

New defence companies often struggle to gain traction as they take on vested interests with new technologies and can run into significant hurdles delivering their products, especially in big quantities.

Covenant said it deliberately avoided sole-source suppliers, lining up three solid-rocket-motor providers with a fourth in the works, and locking in long-term agreements for more than 4,000 jet engines over the next two years.
The company's Dallas plant, spanning 105,000 square feet, opens on Wednesday and is expected to reach full-rate production of 5,000 missiles a year.
Covenant operates a similar-sized facility in Saxony, Germany, which will also have a 5,000-unit-per-year capacity. A smaller site in northern Israel will make 2,000 units a year.--REUTERS
25f455f58a8f5b4b: DEVIGHAT: With roads and bridges destroyed and helicopters busy with search and rescue operations after last month's devastating floods, Nepal's army is turning to drones to deliver relief to displaced people.

Drones are used over distances of up to 3 to 4 kilometres and can haul up to 60 kilogrammes at a time and they are already making an impact for affected communities in dire need of aid, he said.
The army is now making around 10-16 aid deliveries a day with a fleet of four DJI FlyCart 100 drones, all donated from China as part of a recent aid package.

In addition to aid delivery, drones have also been used to move the bodies of flood victims in some affected areas, while reconnaissance drones have also been heavily used in search and rescue operations.

"We've been operating back and forth early in the morning. So yes, it is quite hectic, because we need to have this thing right now," said Milan Pandey of the drone operating company, Airlift Technology.
"Nepal has this geography, this terrain where drones would be really faster, quicker and cheaper," Pandey said.

3b70199cd7b9c88f: MANILA: The Philippine Supreme Court tossed out a graft case against former first lady Imelda Marcos that had languished in the courts for years, documents released on Wednesday show.

Marcos, 97, fled to the United States in 1986 with husband Ferdinand Marcos, who, along with his cronies, was accused of pilfering US$10 billion from the Philippines after a people's uprising ended his 20-year rule.
The former dictator died in 1989 while still in exile, but his heirs later returned to the country, allowing Imelda to see son Ferdinand Marcos Jr. become the country's president in 2022.

The 2018 verdict from the anti-graft Sandiganbayan court had ordered her to serve a minimum of six years behind bars over charges that the Marcoses funnelled roughly US$200 million through Swiss foundations decades ago.
The former first lady, famed for her lavish lifestyle, swiftly filed an appeal.
On Wednesday, court documents revealed the Supreme Court dismissed the case more than two months ago.
"In sum, the relevant Swiss documents were not properly authenticated," the court said in its ruling dated June 10.
"The prosecution was not able to present any credible witness who could have attested to the genuineness and due execution of the documents."
The case is not the first against Imelda Marcos to be overturned by the Supreme Court.
In 1993, it overturned a 24-year jail sentence – also on graft charges. She went on to run for Congress and win while her appeal was underway.

The family's notoriety stems back to Ferdinand Marcos declaring martial law in 1972. That allowed him to shutter the legislature, muzzle the free press and jail or kill those who dared to oppose his dictatorship.
In the decades since Marcos's ouster, the effort to recover the pilfered money has been halting and uneven.--AFP

"I shared a real-life example that occurred just a few weeks ago, the arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of smuggling various types of drugs estimated to be worth RM45 million," he said in a Facebook post.
Saifuddin said the Indonesian National Police shared information about the case.
Following joint action and follow-up, six syndicate members were arrested in Malaysia, including four who had fled to Thailand and Vietnam.
"This is the reality of crime today. The syndicate moved across at least four countries, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Vietnam," he said.

He added that security threats were increasingly complex, including violence, human trafficking, migrant smuggling, narcotics, cybercrime, online scams and money laundering operating through the same cross-border networks, financial systems and digital infrastructure.

He said technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), encrypted communications and cryptocurrencies were also being exploited by criminals to conceal their identities and transfer illicit funds across multiple jurisdictions.
"Crime knows no borders. Our response must not stop at national borders either," he said.
For that reason, Saifuddin said Malaysia continued to strengthen cooperation with China through the Agreement on Cooperation in Preventing and Combating Transnational Crime signed in June 2024.
He said the agreement provided a solid foundation for joint action, including information sharing, operational coordination and investigations.
He said the need was urgent as Malaysia investigated 141,107 online scam cases between 2024 and May 2026.

In narcotics enforcement, Saifuddin said cooperation and intelligence sharing with China helped facilitate two operations in August 2025, which led to the seizure of more than one tonne of fentanyl citrate in Malaysia.
He said bilateral cooperation must translate into strengthening regional security, including through initiatives driven by Malaysia when the nation served as Asean Chairman in 2025.

"The Home Ministry led six major Asean meeting series involving approximately 600 delegates. Among the crucial outcomes were the Asean Plan of Action in Combating Transnational Crime 2026–2035, Melaka Declaration on Combatting Transnational Crime, Asean Declaration on Countering People Smuggling, Asean Declaration on Combatting Cybercrime and Online Scams, as well as the Asean Border Management Cooperation Roadmap," he said.

According to him, Malaysia would continue to play a constructive, reliable and results-oriented security partner alongside China, Asean member states, partners across Asia and the international community.

On technology, Saifuddin said advancements in the field must be harnessed to strengthen security institutions that were professional, accountable and trusted by the people, rather than merely chasing sophistication.

"Because ultimately, when nations and enforcement agencies share information, build trust, and act together, the space for criminal syndicates to operate becomes smaller. When we cooperate, criminals lose," he said. -- BERNAMA

a753f1c1842f31d7: Google plans to invest at least €13 billion ($15 billion) in digital infrastructure and supporting projects in Finland over the next two years. The cloud and search services giant says it is deepening its long-term commitment to Finland and to Europe through additional datacenters and investments in low-carbon electricity generation, onshore wind, and battery storage. Google already has a massive campus at Hamina, on Finland's south coast, which houses seven separate data halls. This is just along the coast from Loviisa, where one of Finland's two operating nuclear power plants is sited. The firm says it intends to expand its facilities at Hamina, but is also constructing new datacenters at sites near Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala, further north in the country. However, it declined to specify how many facilities it is building, or how much extra infrastructure capacity the projects will add to Google's global network. Google said it chose the sites after consulting Business Finland and grid operator Fingrid, focusing on locations in northern and central Finland with existing grid infrastructure and access to carbon-free electricity. Local energy partnerships also form part of the Chocolate Factory's plans. It has signed a 22-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Fortum to support the extension and upgrade of the energy company's Loviisa nuclear plant. Fortum said the plant could not continue operating beyond 2030 without this investment. The Google agreement provides revenue certainty for that work, which is intended to keep the plant – currently responsible for about 10 percent of Finland's electricity – operating through 2050. According to Reuters, the agreement will give Google access to as much as 50 percent of the plant's generating capacity. Fortum said the deal will begin at a lower level in 2028 before reaching 50 percent from 2030 through 2049, which Google confirmed to The Register. The cloud and search firm says it has secured additional onshore wind PPAs with green energy firms Valorem and Suomen Hyötytuuli, bringing the new-to-the-grid onshore wind capacity it has contracted in Finland to 629 MW. Google has also contracted for a 94 MW battery system near its Kajaani site, which is expected to connect to the grid in late 2027. The system is intended to balance supply and reduce price volatility during cold, windless periods. "This investment underscores Google's commitment to grow our presence responsibly, pairing the expansion of our technical infrastructure with new energy capacity, grid enhancements, and energy affordability initiatives," commented Ruth Porat, president and chief investment officer of Alphabet and Google. Google did not answer when The Register asked why it had chosen Finland for this expansion. Obvious attractions include its extensive carbon-free electricity supply – almost 96 percent of the country's generation is described as carbon-neutral – as well as established grid infrastructure near the selected sites. ®
c2b256f675b56211: ASAD Dandia was 8 when he watched the Sept 11, 2001 attacks on television at his Pakistani immigrant parents' home in New York.
Then came the backlash — years of Islamophobia as Americans processed attacks that had killed nearly 3,000 people.
There was anger, suspicion and worse.
At 19, Dandia experienced a police informant posing as a friend to infiltrate his family home, part of a now-disgraced surveillance effort purportedly seeking to detect Islamic extremism.
Today, though, the 33-year-old historian finds a New York transformed: one with its first Muslim mayor, public prayers in Times Square and new mosques rising across the city.
"Twenty-five years after 9/11, we mourn and we grieve what happened. At the same time, we recognise that I am not responsible for what happened.
"I don't deserve to be targeted for what happened and I am as much of a New Yorker as anybody else in that respect," said Dandia, who leads walking tours centred on the city's Muslim communities.
Islamophobia surged in the United States after the 2001 attacks in which militants hijacked airliners and flew them into Manhattan's World Trade Centre and the Pentagon outside Washington.
A fourth plane crashed into a Pennsylvania field after a passenger revolt.
Muslims reported increased public assaults and harassment. Some stopped wearing visual markers such as hijabs to conceal their religion.
Meanwhile, US authorities monitored Muslims by requiring thousands of men and boys to register with the government, leading to many being deported from the country.
"Everyone was in such fear," said Pakistan-born Mohammad Razvi, who founded the Council of Peoples Organisation nonprofit to support Muslims in New York after 9/11.
"We had gunshots fired in our neighbourhood by individuals who felt we were responsible."
He said he started introducing himself as "Mo" after 9/11 to avoid the stigma he encountered when saying "Mohammad".
In New York, police began surveilling hundreds of Muslims as part of their counterterrorism strategy, often targeting people without evidence of wrongdoing.
Dandia experienced this as a college student at 19, when a young Bangladeshi man joined a mutual aid charity he had started.

The pair grew close. Sharing meals, playing sports and even sleeping at Dandia's home. But seven months later, the man revealed that he was a New York City Police Department (NYPD) informant sent to monitor Dandia and his community.
"It was heartbreaking, but it was also terrifying. My relationship with the world around me shifted underneath my feet."
After his ordeal, Dandia and rights groups won a landmark legal settlement that restricted the NYPD from launching similar surveillance programs and established a watchdog to monitor the force.
For Gadier Abbas, an attorney with the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the NYPD programme was the prime example of the "anti-Muslim hysteria" that followed 9/11.
But today, Abbas said, "there is a lot of hope".
"You see American Muslims in every single walk of life, almost at every single level and that's a testament to the vibrancy of the community."
New York will soon boast the largest mosque in the state — one of more than 100 added since 2001 in New York — while Muslims are a rising cultural and political force.
Still, Islamophobia persists in the city where around nine per cent of the population is Muslim.
In March, a far-right influencer organised a "Stop the Islamic Takeover of New York City" rally outside the mayor's residence.
A conservative senator said Mayor Zohran Mamdani should be sent to Guantanamo Bay, the US detention camp best known for holding 9/11 suspects.

Rudy Giuliani, who was mayor of the city during the attacks, said it "offends me" that Mamdani will attend the 9/11 memorial service. Some relatives of victims have called for him to stay away, while other families have defended the mayor.
Dandia acknowledged Islamophobia had not disappeared, but he was optimistic about how far New York's Muslim community has come.
"I've seen the growth of our institutional power, but also the recognition by other New Yorkers who are not Muslim, that we are all part of this city together."
The writer is from AFP

278a7c9abe4e0870: WASHINGTON: Meta said Wednesday it had begun testing Community Notes in 16 Spanish-speaking countries in Latin America, a step toward replacing the professional fact-checking programme it runs with partner organisations across the region.

The crowdsourced notes system, modelled on the one used by Elon Musk's X, is designed to supplant checks carried out by accredited newsrooms and fact-checking agencies, which Meta ended in the US last year.
Meta said it hoped the notes would become the standard way it adds context to misleading posts on Facebook, Instagram and Threads, ending the need for the fact-checking programme.
The company gave no timeline for that transition, saying only that full rollout would come when it was confident the product worked.

Users in the 16 countries can sign up as contributors from Tuesday, but Meta said no notes would be visible to the public during the test and that independent fact-checking would continue unchanged in the meantime.
The list covers Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay and Venezuela.
Brazil, the region's largest market for Meta's platforms, was left out.
The head of the world's main fact-checking network said she was "deeply concerned" by Meta's decision.

"The community notes program alone is simply not adequate when it comes to reducing the impact of harmful falsehoods on social media platforms," Angie Holan, director of the International Fact-Checking Network, of which AFP is a member, said in a statement.
Right-wing surge
The announcement lands after a run of elections that has pushed Latin America sharply toward right-wing parties.
Hard-right conservatives, including in the US and Europe, are largely against fact-checking programs on social media, accusing them of political bias.
Far-right politician Jose Antonio Kast won Chile's runoff in December before taking office in March, and this year Peru and Colombia both elected right-wing presidents.
Argentina's libertarian President Javier Milei, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, strengthened his hand in last year's midterms.

Just days before Trump took office for a second term, Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg announced that the company would end its US fact-checking partnerships and replace them with Community Notes.
In line with Republican views, Zuckerberg cast the shift as a return to free expression.
Testing began in the US that March. Three weeks later the notes started appearing publicly and the US fact-checking program was shut down.
Meta said Tuesday that the US program now had more than 1.4 million contributors and that the daily volume of notes had overtaken what fact-checkers produced, often faster.
Last year, the company pointed to a far thinner output of roughly 70,000 contributors who wrote 15,000 notes over six months.

Meta's Oversight Board, the quasi-independent body the company funds to review its moderation decisions, warned in March that Community Notes were not an adequate replacement for professional fact-checking outside the US.
It said a global rollout risked human rights harms in politically polarized countries and during tense elections.
AFP is among the fact-checking organizations that participate in Meta's program in Latin America and elsewhere.
Phil Chetwynd, AFP's global news director, said the news agency's verification teams in the region had delivered "outstanding work" over eight years that Meta itself had praised.
He said the two systems should not be treated as alternatives.

"Credible research suggests that community notes can only be effective when contributors can rely on accurate, ethically produced, fact-checked journalism and other high-quality sources when drafting their notes," Chetwynd said.
"Fact-checking and community notes should go hand in hand. What matters is the quality of the notes, not their quantity."
c4e34a56864db8c4: PRIME Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to consolidate Israel's fractious right-wing parties ahead of a Tuesday deadline to avoid an election loss forecast by opinion polls.

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, is seeking a record seventh term in the Oct 27 election, but he has faced pressure over the Hamas-led 2023 attack on Israel and subsequent wars in Gaza, Iran and Lebanon.
Surveys have for months been pointing to a defeat for his nationalist-religious coalition.
Netanyahu has, therefore, been pressing allies to merge their candidate lists and raise their chances of gaining Parliament seats, so far with only partial success.
"When we unite, we win. When we splinter, we lose," he said in an Aug 30 interview on Channel 14, a pro-Netanyahu television station.
"I am doing all I can, as I did in the previous election, to unite these parties."

No single party has ever won an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset, Israel's Parliament, making coalition governments the norm and sometimes giving as many as a dozen parties a chance of winning seats.
To do so, they must pass a 3.25 per cent vote threshold, equal to four seats, meaning smaller parties risk drawing votes without gaining a seat.
Polls suggest that Netanyahu's Likud party stands to lose a third of its parliamentary power.

Though it may still remain the largest party, winning 20-23 seats, Netanyahu would likely need his coalition allies, including the far-right Jewish Power and Religious Zionism parties, to remain in office.
Religious Zionism, led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, has been polling between zero and six seats, down from seven.
With Netanyahu's blessing, it merged its list on Sept 1 with that of Zehut, a small party headed by former far-right libertarian and Likud member, Moshe Feiglin.
But National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has rebuffed Netanyahu's calls for his Jewish Power party, which holds six seats, to run with Religious Zionism, as it did in the last election.
Ben-Gvir has argued that the parties would be stronger running separately.
Feiglin's views on the Palestinians are similar to those of Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, whose calls to annex the occupied West Bank and depopulate Gaza have drawn international ire.

Though such foreign criticism may have little impact on the vote, another worry for Netanyahu is political newcomer Ofer Winter, a right-wing former brigadier-general whose views are largely aligned with those of Smotrich.
But Winter has rejected calls to merge his party, saying he will not run with anyone who may be responsible for the security failure that allowed for the 2023 Hamas-led attack.
Winter has cast the election as a protest vote and says he will draw right-wingers who are seeking a fresh start. Latest polls show him at four seats or none.
"He chose to go separately and we are now in danger," Netanyahu told Channel 14, arguing that he risks "wasting" crucial right-wing votes if he does not win enough seats to enter the Knesset.

The parliamentary system delivered a decisive victory for Netanyahu in the 2022 election, when a splintered centre-left was knocked out by a unified right-wing alliance. Now, however, Israel's most dominant politician of his generation is in a far weaker starting position.
Netanyahu's hawkish image was shattered by the security failing of the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack and by wars in Gaza, Iran and Lebanon that brought military successes but no lasting victories.

"He has never faced anything like what he faces now. Everyone in Israel shares a sense of historical crisis and his name is all over it. And he knows this," said Amotz Asa-El, a political analyst with the Shalom Hartman Institute in Jerusalem.
Netanyahu's strongest rival at the moment is Gadi Eisenkot, Israel's former military chief, who lost a son in Gaza.
His Yashar party has been on a steady rise for months, matching and sometimes overtaking Likud in the polls, though his path to power is still unclear.
Netanyahu's age is a factor too, said Asa-El.
"When he first ran in '96, he was the Israeli Kennedy. Now he's running as the Israeli Biden."
The writer is from Reuters

a8925e6e46d8a24b: PORT KLANG: Two Indonesian women allegedly paid between RM200 and RM250 for fake copies of Malaysian identity cards to help them secure jobs after entering the country illegally.

The women, both aged 37, were among three Indonesians detained on suspicion of using fake copies of identity cards or documents belonging to other individuals during Ops Layar at a printing factory in Bandar Sultan Suleiman here today.
One of them, identified as Lifa from Sulawesi, claimed she paid about RM200 for the identification document after entering Malaysia through an illegal route in June.
"I came here just to earn money. I didn't know what I was doing was an offence," she said.
Lifa, who was paid her wages in cash, said she had given her photograph to the person who prepared the document.
"I gave my photograph to the person who made the document and they replaced the photograph on the identity card with mine.
"I only obtained the copy of the identity card to look for work. I just wanted to earn money and didn't know that what I was doing was an offence," she said after the operation.
Another woman, identified as Rini from West Java, claimed she paid about RM250 to an acquaintance introduced by a fellow Indonesian for a fake copy of an identity card.
Rini said she had been living in Malaysia since 2022 after entering the country illegally.
She said she previously worked at a grocery store before taking up a job at the printing factory, where she was paid about RM95 a day.
"I had previously been deported from Malaysia and my passport was blacklisted, but I later re-entered through an illegal route after paying about six million rupiah," she said.
She told officers there that she used the fake identity card copy to make it easier for her to secure employment.

National Registration Department (NRD) Putrajaya Enforcement Division director Mazhad Abdul Aziz said Ops Layar was mounted following a month-long intelligence operation to identify individuals suspected of misusing identification documents.

He said 67 enforcement personnel were involved in the operation, comprising 52 NRD officers from Putrajaya, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, 10 Immigration Department officers from Putrajaya and five Selangor Labour Department officers.
"A total of 195 individuals were inspected, including 63 Malaysians who possessed valid identity cards.

"Three women aged between 21 and 37, believed to be Indonesian nationals, were detained on suspicion of using fake copies of identity cards or those belonging to other individuals to secure employment," he said.
Mazhad said the case was being investigated under Regulation 25(1)(e) of the National Registration Regulations 1990 (Amendment 2007).
Those convicted face up to three years' imprisonment, a fine of up to RM20,000, or both.
Mazhad said the NRD conducted 738 enforcement operations between January and Aug 31 this year, resulting in 365 arrest and prosecution cases.
Of these, 286 involved offences under the National Registration Regulations 1990 related to the use of fake identity cards and identity cards belonging to other people.
Another 79 cases involved fake birth certificates under the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1957 (Act 299).
During the same operation, the Immigration Department inspected 129 individuals and detained six for suspected offences under the Immigration Act.
"Todays operation shows how effective our operations have been. We were quite excited to see so few offences committed today," he said.

2712e902a35fbe8a: THE helicopter crash at Long Lellang is a particularly tragic reminder of the risks some healthcare workers take to simply to reach Malaysians who live far from hospitals and clinics.
There is especially a painful irony in the tragedy: those who were flying into the interior to care for others became victims themselves.
The selflessness of the healthcare workers who undertake difficult assignments ensures that people in remote areas are not forgotten.
It must be acknowledged that access to healthcare is not simply a matter of building hospitals. In Sarawak, geography makes alternative forms of delivery — including air services — essential.

At the same time, the tragedy must prompt careful examination of the conditions under which such essential services are delivered to remote areas: aircraft, operators, landing facilities and communication facilities and emergency response. The response must also recognise the communities it was trying to reach.
The answer cannot be to retreat from difficult-to-reach areas because providing healthcare there is hazardous or expensive.

If anything, the tragedy should strengthen the commitment that people in remote areas receive the same standard of healthcare as those in urban centres — while making the journey safer for the personnel who deliver it.

Here, too, much work needs to be done. We are not so good at building our own databases. For the longest time, we have been working with what others provide us. The simple truth is that what you can't measure, you can't manage.
The Long Lellang helicopter crash on Tuesday that claimed the lives of five is fresh in the people's minds.

Many remember the tragedy but as usual the crash will disappear in the mists of past. How many such crashes happened in the past in Sarawak or Sabah, two parts of Malaysia with difficult terrain? We can't say for sure that the terrain was a contributing factor or a risk factor for helicopter crashes.

The official investigation by Malaysia's Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) is underway. The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia has confirmed that the Bo 105 was conducting a Flying Doctor Service when it crashed near Long Lellang short take-off and landing airport.
Steep hills and mountainous terrain leave pilots very few escape routes. Similarly, forced landings are near impossibility in such terrains.

A series of causes can be listed for the helicopter crash but that will be like putting the cart before the horse. We will do well to wait for the full report of the AAIB. Everything else will be speculative.
This is a moment first for mourning, not recrimination. But once the grief has settled, there must be a sober examination of what can be done to make medical outreach missions safer.
70c4afd2d9e3a050: PETALING JAYA: A stench emanating from a house at Taman Seri Bistari in Nibong Tebal, Penang, led to the discovery of a dead man in a sewage tank with his hands and feet bound.

fc0c46663d1baea4: The UK government has told MPs that Fujitsu has promised not to pursue contracts with new public sector customers through frameworks potentially worth billions of pounds while its voluntary bidding moratorium remains in place. In July, The Register revealed that the Japanese supplier had won a place on a UK government framework worth up to £14.9 billion despite its role in the Post Office Horizon scandal, one of the greatest miscarriages of justice in modern times. The supplier's place on the Digital Outcomes and Specialists 7 (DOS7) framework came after it won spots on two other frameworks, including Technology Services 4, worth up to £19.08 billion, and Transport Technology worth around £2.3 billion. In January 2024, Fujitsu voluntarily committed to stop bidding for contracts with new government customers until the public inquiry into the Horizon scandal had concluded. After Fujitsu secured places on the three government frameworks, House of Commons Business and Trade Committee chair Liam Byrne wrote to the government seeking assurance that the company would not use them to pursue work from new public sector customers. He also asked what discussions the government had held with Fujitsu about its participation and compliance with the moratorium. Horizon is an EPOS and back-end finance system that was first implemented in the 1990s by ICL, a UK tech firm majority-owned by Fujitsu at the time and fully acquired in 1998. It has since undergone two upgrades. Between 1999 and 2015, the Post Office prosecuted 700 subpostmasters in cases in which Horizon evidence may have featured, while almost 300 more cases were brought by other bodies. Hundreds were wrongfully convicted, devastating lives in the process. A statutory inquiry into the scandal was launched in 2021 and remains ongoing. The inquiry's first report said the families of at least 13 people believed their deaths by suicide were linked to their experiences with Horizon and the Post Office. Fujitsu has apologized for its role in the scandal. Frameworks are procurement vehicles that let public bodies buy from pre-approved suppliers under agreed terms, although a place on one does not guarantee any work. The Government Commercial Agency (GCA) – which replaced the Crown Commercial Service – is the Cabinet Office agency that manages the framework and receives a 1 percent levy on sales made through it. In a letter published this week, Cabinet Office Parliamentary Secretary Mark Ferguson said: "While appointment to a GCA framework, such as DOS7, places a supplier on a list of approved providers, Fujitsu has assured the GCA that its voluntary moratorium fully applies to call-off contract opportunities that arise via its participation on GCA frameworks. Consequently, inclusion on a framework does not override Fujitsu's commitment not to seek work with new public sector customers." He added that the GCA monitors Fujitsu's compliance with its self-imposed bidding restrictions and that agency officials were in regular contact with the company to oversee its framework activity. "To date, GCA can confirm that Fujitsu have kept to these self-imposed restrictions," Ferguson wrote. In April 2025, The Register revealed that Fujitsu had won a £125 million contract to build Northern Ireland's new land registry system for the Department of Finance, a new government customer, more than a year after its voluntary moratorium came into effect. At the time, a spokesperson for Fujitsu told The Register: "Fujitsu was named preferred bidder for this contract in 2023, before the voluntary restrictions came into place." Fujitsu's 2024 letter said the company would assess its continued involvement in procurements that were already underway when the moratorium began. However, it also said Fujitsu would bid for work with a new government customer only if asked to do so. Fujitsu said it had been named preferred bidder for the Northern Ireland contract before introducing the restrictions. The Northern Ireland government subsequently confirmed to The Register that it had not asked the company to continue bidding. Ferguson's letter does not explain how that award was reconciled with Fujitsu's undertaking. The Register has asked the Cabinet Office for clarification. ®

8e4df18e9932982b: MANCHESTER: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United are strong enough to compete with Europe's best on their return to the Champions League for the first time in three years.
Carrick earned his position as permanent United boss after leading the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League in his interim spell last season.
Having secured a place in Europe's elite club competition, United kick off their league phase campaign on Thursday when they face Azerbaijani champions Sabah at Old Trafford.

"It's a magical competition. It's where we all want to be. When you're out of it, you realise how special it is and when you're in it, you want to make the most of it," Carrick told reporters on Wednesday.
"I think we've all seen some special, special nights and felt some special things in this competition over the years. It's the best competition to challenge yourself and to push against the best.
"We're delighted to be here, but we're not here to just enjoy the occasion. We're here to do business and go as far as we possibly can."
In two of their last three appearances in the Champions League, the three-time European champions have crashed out at the group stage and have not progressed beyond the last 16 since 2019.
United have also made a slow start to the Premier League season, taking just four points from fixtures against Hull, Ipswich and Everton.
However, many of their better performances under Carrick have come against stronger opposition.
United beat Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea in the second half of last season.
"I think we're capable of doing some really good things in this competition and going further down the line in this competition," Carrick said.
"Certainly not getting ahead of ourselves because some part of it is a new experience for some of the players.
"But the boys are used to playing European football for the most part in different competitions and we'll take that forward and we've got a squad that's strong enough to compete."
In contrast to the record-setting spending by many of their Premier League rivals, United were only able to strengthen their midfield in the transfer window.
United benefited last season from only playing 40 games – their lowest total since the 1914/15 campaign.
Carrick, though, said his players had to embrace the challenge of a heavier workload.
"We play Thursday, Sunday, Wednesday and it's what we're here for. It's about managing the group and having trust in everyone able to play," he said.
Benjamin Sesko is in contention for his first start of the season after coming off the bench to score in Sunday's 2-2 draw at Everton.
Carrick confirmed Matthijs de Ligt is also nearing a comeback after nearly a year out with a back injury.

bf21e7d88aaa2ae7: JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said during a visit to Israeli troops in southern Syria on Wednesday that Iran's Islamic republic was on the verge of collapse as fighting in the six-month Middle East war intensifies.

"There is still work to be done – the main task is to bring down the terror regime in Iran. We are very close to that. We know that the entire axis will ultimately collapse," he said on the Syrian side of Mount Hermon on the Israel-Syria border during a visit with defence minister Israel Katz.
In southern Syria, Israeli forces have been stationed in a "security zone" since the fall of long-time ruler Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.
They occupy what was previously a buffer zone patrolled by the United Nations that had separated Israeli and Syrian forces in the Israeli-occupied Golan since 1974.
"We will not allow any terrorist army to establish itself on our border," Netanyahu reiterated on Wednesday.

Katz visited Israeli troops stationed in southern Syria two weeks ago, prompting condemnation from Damascus, which denounced a "flagrant violation of the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity".
Israel has carried out hundreds of strikes in Syria since the fall of Assad and made repeated incursions into Syrian territory.
Officials have also repeatedly vowed to keep troops in the security zone, where Israel is seeking a broader demilitarised area.

Netanyahu's threats against Iran come as Tehran and Washington are locked in a stalemate over the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with both sides trading attacks in the past week, six months into the war that the US and Israel launched against the Islamic Republic at the end of February.
acb5b2c2b87bf6c3: PETALING JAYA: The Kangar Bersatu division committee, along with leaders of its youth and women’s wings and “90 branch chiefs”, have left the party to join Wawasan.

The latest defections come a day after Padang Besar Bersatu deputy chief Ramzi Udi and 19 other party leaders and members announced their departure from the party, citing dissatisfaction with its leadership.
In a statement today, Kangar Bersatu deputy chief Faisol Rahman said the group had chosen to leave Bersatu “amicably and with dignity” after a loss of confidence in the party’s central leadership.
He said Bersatu’s direction, organisational management and leadership approach did not meet their expectations as division and branch leaders.
Faisol said the group would join Wawasan because they believed its direction and leadership were more closely aligned with the aspirations and needs of the grassroots.
“We believe the strength of any political party begins with trust between its leadership and the grassroots. When that trust has eroded, we feel the time has come to take a clear stand.
“We are leaving Bersatu because we have lost confidence. We are joining Wawasan because we believe in a new direction,” he said.
Faisol said the defections involved 90 of the 99 Kangar division branch chiefs. He also said the move did not involve any Bersatu MP or assemblyman in Perlis.
He said the Hujong Tanjung branch, headed by Perlis menteri besar Abu Bakar Hamzah, would remain with Bersatu.
The developments follow the appointment of Padang Besar Bersatu chief Izizam Ibrahim as the party’s new Perlis chief.
Bersatu secretary-general Azmin Ali said the appointment, approved by party president Muhyiddin Yassin, took effect on Sept 3.
Perlis Bersatu was previously led by Abu Bakar, who is also the Kuala Perlis assemblyman.
Abu Bakar resigned from Bersatu’s Supreme Council on July 9.

0e405640a25d9cf9: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is all for greater Malay unity, but those seeking to cooperate with the Barisan Nasional linchpin must accept its centrist and moderate approach, Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
The Umno deputy president said the party would not allow its political partners to impose radical or conservative ideologies on it.

"Umno will always be centrist. Our ideology is centrism. Umno is a group and a movement in the middle and will always follow the middle path," Mohamad said in his speech when he simultaneously launched the Wanita Umno, Umno Youth and Puteri Umno delegates' conferences here today.
Mohamad said Umno would not lean to the left or right, but would seek to balance ideas from across the political spectrum as a moderate national party.
"We will not lean to the left or the right. Our commitment is to balance ideas from the left and right as a moderate national party," he said.
He said Umno's position had been tested over decades through its role in governing the country with moderate policies, priorities and approaches.
"As such, anyone who wants to cooperate with Umno must accept Umno's moderation and centrist position.
"You cannot force your conservative or radical ideology on Umno," he said.
Mohamad said Umno's approach to Malay politics would also remain inclusive, with Malays serving as the "mother race" providing space and opportunities for all Malaysians.
He said the party would work towards ensuring Malaysia remained a prosperous country that was managed responsibly and in line with the Federal Constitution.
"To my non-Malay friends and non-Muslim Bumiputera friends in Sabah and Sarawak, Umno's pledge is for a just and united Malaysia," he said.
Mohamad said Umno's approach to Malay politics would be mature and should not become a burden or threat to other communities, nor deny their rights and interests.
"We will manage Malay politics maturely and it will in no way become a burden or threat, or deny your rights and interests."
He said the Malaysia envisioned by Umno was one that was peaceful, prosperous and based on mutual respect and complementarity among all communities.
f9bf465aeab331a3: MARAN: Thick smoke engulfed the paediatric and women's wards at Jengka Hospital here as 17 patients, including 11 children, were evacuated to safety after a fire damaged their ceilings.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said police were alerted to the fire at the hospital building at 7pm.
Several images of the incident showing thick smoke engulfing the premises went viral on social media, raising concerns about the safety of patients.
In another video, hospital staff were seen wheeling patients on hospital beds out of the building to safety, while firefighters were seen rushing into the burning premises.
The beds were later arranged along the hospital corridor.
The 6.50pm fire damaged parts of the ceiling and wiring at both wards.
"Firefighters managed to put out the fire within 20 minutes. The fire is believed to have started in the ceiling of the paediatric and women's wards," Wong said in a statement today.
He said 11 children, six boys and five girls, and six women who were warded at the premises escaped unhurt after they were evacuated to safety.
Wong said checks by firemen revealed that the fire had damaged about 10 per cent of the ceiling.
"The cause of the fire and the losses incurred are still under investigation," he said.
Meanwhile, a Fire and Rescue Department spokesman said 12 firefighters from the Jengka and Kuala Krau fire stations were deployed to put out the fire.
5549c3da6f5e4fbe: SINGAPORE: DBS Bank is being sued for an estimated S$1.298 billion (US$1.03 billion) in damages linked to the multibillion-dollar 1MDB scandal, Southeast Asia's largest lender, DBS Group, said on Wednesday.
The claimants include the liquidators of four companies - BlackRock Commodities (Global), Platinum Global Luxury Services, Affinity Equity International Partners, and TKIL Global Investments.
The liquidators did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
DBS rejected the claim and said it would fight it vigorously, adding that the company has made no provision for the lawsuit. The bank did not provide any more details on the allegations it faces.

The lawsuit is the latest among wide-ranging efforts to recover money belonging to 1MDB, from which US investigators say about US$4.5 billion was stolen between 2009 and 2014 in a complex, globe-spanning scheme.
All this time, there was no claim against DBS, according to the lender's statement.

In July last year, liquidators trying to recover money from 1MDB sued Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore, alleging that it enabled fraud that led to more than US$2.7 billion in financial losses between 2009 and 2013.
Shares of DBS closed 0.8% lower at S$77.50 earlier in the day.
5bdc581aa9ff7c99: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno kekal sebagai parti berhaluan tengah untuk semua rakyat Malaysia, bukan hanya orang Melayu, kata Timbalan Presidennya Mohamad Hasan.

810b0b67523aa7fe: GENEVA: The UN on Wednesday decried a "deafening" international silence over Afghanistan's deepening rights and humanitarian crisis and demanded a halt to forced returns to the country.

Countries must renew efforts to pressure Afghanistan's Taliban government to end a raft of oppressive restrictions imposed on women and girls in particular, UN rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement.
"Today, the plight of many in Afghanistan is going from bad to worse," he said.

"Millions are mired in poverty, respect for basic human rights continues to deteriorate as hundreds of thousands are being returned against their will" from countries where they sought refuge, he added.
"Yet, it seems the world has forgotten and abandoned the people of Afghanistan to a plight deepening by the day. The silence is deafening."
Under the Taliban, women are banned from public places, including parks, and from most jobs, while education for girls beyond age 12 is outlawed.
Around 2.4 million girls in Afghanistan have been denied access to secondary education since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, according to the UN.
Turk warned that fresh decrees this year were making "it more difficult for a woman to separate from a spouse and implicitly authorise child marriage and violence against women and children".
"Such restrictions imposed on women and girls – which amount to gender apartheid – have no place in any society."
The UN rights office also highlighted numerous arrests of both men and women by the Taliban over alleged violations of restrictions such as dress code, beard length and playing or listening to music.
At least 449 men and women had been subjected to corporal punishment in just the first half of this year, it found.
It pointed to violations against religious minorities, former government officials and former members of the country's defence and security forces.
Turk complained that forced returns to Afghanistan were continuing despite the horrific rights situation and as "foreign aid flows have trickled dry, compounding the misery".
According to the UN refugee agency, more than 400,000 Afghans have been forcibly returned so far this year, mainly from Iran and Pakistan, but also from several European Union states.
"I implore all states to reconsider their actions and to put the lives of the suffering population first," Turk said.

Saifuddin berkata demikian mengulas kenyataan Asyraf Wajdi yang mendakwa kenyataan Majlis Setiausaha PH, yang menegaskan mereka yang disabitkan atas kesalahan rasuah atau salah guna kuasa, khususnya dalam kes berprofil tinggi, perlu menjalani tempoh hukuman sepenuhnya, seolah-olah mempertikaikan kuasa perlembagaan Agong untuk memberikan pengampunan.
Mengulas lanjut Saifuddin berkata, kenyataan PH itu langsung tidak menyentuh mana-mana parti politik atau kes yang berkaitan dengannya.
“Jangan ubah persoalan tentang rasuah menjadi drama kononnya derhaka kepada Raja. Itu dua perkara yang berbeza.
"Institusi Raja mesti terus dihormati, manakala rasuah tetap wajib ditentang. Tidak ada kompromi di antara kedua-duanya,” katanya.
Beliau turut meminta Umno supaya berhenti menuduh PH meremehkan institusi diraja, sebaliknya parti itu perlu menjawab isu di Negeri Sembilan.
“Jangan hanya lantang bercakap soal Raja apabila ia menguntungkan naratif politik sendiri, tetapi membisu apabila timbul persoalan yang jauh lebih serius di depan mata.
"Hormati Raja dengan mempertahankan Perlembagaan secara konsisten, bukannya menggunakan sentimen terhadap institusi diraja untuk menutup perbahasan tentang rasuah dan integriti,” katanya.

Terdahulu media melaporkan Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan dijangka bersidang pada Jumaat untuk mempertimbangkan, antara lainnya, permohonan bekas perdana Menteri Najib Razak untuk mendapatkan pengampunan terhadap sabitan berkaitan skandal 1MDB.
adf22e71cc5e8cf5: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno remains a centrist party for all Malaysians, not just the Malays, said party deputy president Mohamad Hasan.

Opening the general assemblies of the Umno Youth, Wanita Umno and Puteri Umno wings here tonight, Mohamad said the party would ensure the country was a “homeland for all, prosperous, and carefully managed, in line with the Federal Constitution”.
“We must never think that our constituents consist only of Malays. Our actions and conduct must never create concern among non-Malays and our friends in Sabah and Sarawak,” he said.
Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, reminded delegates that Umno needed the confidence of non-Malays and parties in Sabah and Sarawak to form the government amid “chaotic” Malaysian politics.
“They have now become the deciding forces. The time when we regarded them as fixed deposits is a thing of the past,” he said.
Noting concerns expressed by non-Malays about the country’s direction given the dominance of Malay-Muslim politics, Mohamad said Umno had always been a centrist party.

“Our ideology is centrism. I repeat: Umno will always take the middle path. We will not lean to the left or right. Our commitment is to balance ideas from both the left and right as a moderate national party,” he said.
Mohamad also warned potential partners of Umno against imposing “conservative” or “radical” ideologies on the party.

“For decades, we have managed and governed the country with moderate attitudes, policies, positions and priorities. Therefore, anyone who wishes to cooperate with Umno must accept Umno’s moderate, middle-ground approach,” he said.
4379eb10e1a83f94: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno tidak mahu lagi 'dipermainkan' dalam usaha penyatuan politik Melayu-Islam dan akan lebih berhati-hati terhadap sebarang kerjasama pada masa depan, kata Timbalan Presiden Mohamad Hasan.

Beliau berkata pengalaman berkenaan menyebabkan Umno mengambil pendekatan lebih berhati-hati terhadap sebarang usaha untuk menjalinkan kerjasama atas nama penyatuan Melayu.
